newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hang Seng Bank shares sell-off overdone - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Hang Seng Bank shares sell-off overdone - analysts.

text.p: Blue chip Hang Seng Bank Ltd has seen its share price clobbered after its revelation of disappointing 1996 earnings, but some traders said the gloom was unwarranted.
"All the selling is overdone," said Roland Bruce, assistant director at NAVA SC Securities.
He said the bank's results were disappointing mainly due to two factors: A more than four-fold increase in the level of provisions for bad debts and a sharp fall in the level of exceptional items.
"This large increase in provisions appears to be chiefly for one account and should therefore be a one-off," said Bruce.
The percentage of non-accruing loans on Hang Seng Bank's balance sheet is low for the industry at 0.92 percent of total loans, he added.
On Monday, Hang Seng Bank reported a 6.3 percent rise in earnings for 1996, substantially below the market's consensus forecast of 16 percent.

"I think the numbers were below expectations...and I think that was pretty much the reason for the decline," said Shannon Garrett, banking analyst at SocGen Crosby Securities. "We have downgraded the stock to a hold."
The fall in exceptional items, which in past years have been derived from the sale of listed securities, also came as a surprise to analysts.

In the second half of 1995 and first half of 1996 the bank sold shares in its portfolio, but made no such "investment securities disposals" in the second half of 1996, the company said in its results statement.
"The company said it has HK$5.4 billion in unrealised gains on listed securities," said Alex Wong, banking analyst at Dharmala Securities.
"Management is bullish on the stock market and plans to hold the securities to book higher profits -- this is a positive thing," he said.
Many analysts have revised upwards their 1997 earnings forecasts to an average 17 percent growth.
"We are looking for earnings growth to surge slightly ahead of the market going forward," said Garrett of SocGen Crosby.
Continued good growth in the volume and value of loans was forecast to offset a slight fall in net interest margins, analysts said.
Garrett has forecast earnings growth of 17 percent in 1997 and 15 percent for 1998.
Despite the positive outlook, most analysts think the bank's share price is too high. "Given the current valuation, it will be difficult for the bank to outperform the index," Garrett added.
Based on Garrett's forecast, the shares are trading on a price-to-earnings multiple of 16.2 times 1997 earnings.
In 1996, the share price rose 36 percent, outperforming the Hang Seng Index's 34 percent gain. The share closed HK$0.50 down at HK$83.00 on Thursday.
